ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: First describe the image: the figure is a “statistical chart of urbanization development in the world and four continents”; the horizontal axis includes the world, Asia, Africa, Europe, and North America; columns indicate the urbanization level in 2010, and the line indicates the average urbanization speed. In the figure, the urbanization levels of Asia and Africa are relatively low, but the average urbanization speed is relatively fast; Europe and North America have relatively high urbanization levels, while their urbanization speed is relatively slow. Then reason: emerging countries usually correspond to a stage with a relatively low urbanization level but a relatively fast development speed. Rapid urbanization causes large numbers of rural population and labor force to flow into cities, and cities are more likely to have employment pressure, oversupply of labor, and other problems, rather than labor shortage. Therefore, among the problems appearing in cities, the labor-force condition most inconsistent with reality is “labor shortage.”
